questions.question: Where is `c.Next()` implemented, the call a middleware uses to run the rest of the handler chain before doing its own after-work?
questions.notes: Exact method name; 'Next' is a common word and gin also calls c.Next() in many places. Context.Next increments c.index and loops over c.handlers, calling each non-nil handler and incrementing again, so the code after c.Next() in a middleware runs once the downstream handlers have returned (context.go:197-205). Abort only sets c.index = abortIndex (math.MaxInt8 >> 1, line 57) so the loop stops. handleHTTPRequest starts the chain with c.Next() (gin.go:751, related). Wrong but plausible: Context.Abort / IsAborted (stop the chain), HandlersChain.Last (gin.go:67-72, returns the main handler), serveError (gin.go:793-808, also calls c.Next for the 404/405 chains), the Logger or Recovery closures that call c.Next().

questions.question: I want to keep using the request's context inside a goroutine I start from a handler. Which method gives me a copy of `*gin.Context` that is safe to use there?
questions.notes: Copy builds a new Context that shares Request and engine, detaches the writer (writermem.ResponseWriter = nil), sets index to abortIndex and handlers to nil, and clones Keys under the read lock plus Params, Errors and Accepted (context.go:122-154). It is needed because ServeHTTP takes the Context from engine.pool and puts it back after the request (gin.go:696-703), and reset() clears it for the next request (context.go:103-118). Wrong but plausible: Context.reset (the reuse Copy protects against), Engine.allocateContext (creates pooled contexts), Context.Value / Context.Done (context.Context methods, no copy), Engine.HandleContext.

questions.question: My debug log shows `[WARNING] Headers were already written. Wanted to override status code 200 with 500`. Which code prints that warning, and why is the status not changed?
questions.notes: responseWriter.WriteHeader only records the status; when the code differs from the stored one and Written() is already true (size != noWritten, i.e. WriteHeaderNow or a body write has happened), it calls debugPrint with this warning and returns without changing anything (response_writer.go:67-75). debugPrint prints only in debug mode (debug.go:56-70). Context.Status and the render helpers reach it through c.Writer.WriteHeader (context.go:1122-1124). Wrong but plausible: Context.Status (the caller), debugPrint (only prints), responseWriter.WriteHeaderNow (where the header is actually sent), Context.Render.

questions.question: Where is bracket syntax in the query string, like `ids[a]=1&ids[b]=2`, turned into a map when I call `c.QueryMap("ids")`?
questions.notes: getMapFromFormData scans every key of the parsed values, keeps those that start with key + '[' and contain a closing ']', and stores the text between the brackets as the map key with the first value (context.go:683-704). GetQueryMap feeds it the cached URL query and GetPostFormMap the form cache (related). Wrong but plausible: setFormMap in binding/form_mapping.go:528-550 (binds the whole form into a map[string]string or map[string][]string, no brackets), Context.QueryArray / GetQueryArray (repeated keys, not brackets), initQueryCache (only caches URL.Query()).

questions.question: Registering both `/users/:id` and `/users/:name` panics with "conflicts with existing wildcard". Which function raises that panic?
questions.notes: node.addRoute walks the radix tree; when the new path needs a wildcard where the node already has a wildcard child, it checks that the existing wildcard is a prefix of the new segment and not a catch-all, otherwise it builds "'<segment>' in new path '<full>' conflicts with existing wildcard '<existing>' in existing prefix '<prefix>'" and panics (tree.go:210-234). It also panics with 'handlers are already registered for path' (242-244). Wrong but plausible: node.insertChild (the other registration panics: one wildcard per segment, unnamed wildcard, catch-all position and conflicts, 297-364), findWildcard (only finds and validates the wildcard), Engine.addRoute (asserts, then calls node.addRoute).

questions.question: Recovery middleware'i panic'i loga yazarken isteğin Authorization başlığını nerede gizliyor?
questions.notes: Describes one function in Turkish. secureRequestDump dumps the request with httputil.DumpRequest(r, false), splits it into lines and replaces every line that starts with 'Authorization:' with 'Authorization: *' (recovery.go:98-107). CustomRecoveryWithWriter calls it for the broken-pipe log line and the debug-mode log line (72, 74-75); outside debug mode the request is not dumped at all (77-78). Wrong but plausible: CustomRecoveryWithWriter (the caller), stack (the stack trace), defaultHandleRecovery (writes the 500), BasicAuthForRealm (reads Authorization, does not mask it).

questions.question: BasicAuth middleware'inde gelen Authorization başlığı kayıtlı kullanıcı/şifre çiftleriyle nerede karşılaştırılıyor, karşılaştırma sabit zamanlı mı?
questions.notes: The header is never decoded: processAccounts precomputes 'Basic ' + base64(user:password) for each account (auth.go:76-94), and searchCredential compares the raw Authorization value with each precomputed value using subtle.ConstantTimeCompare and returns the user on a match (32-42), so each comparison is constant-time. BasicAuthForRealm calls it and answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate on failure (48-68, related). Wrong but plausible: BasicAuthForRealm (the middleware wrapper), BasicAuthForProxy (Proxy-Authorization, 98-116), authorizationHeader (builds the expected value, compares nothing).

questions.question: GIN_MODE ortam degiskeni nerede okunuyor, release moduna gecis nasil yapiliyor?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('GIN_MODE ortam değişkeni nerede okunuyor, release moduna geçiş nasıl yapılıyor'). The package init reads os.Getenv(EnvGinMode) and passes it to SetMode (mode.go:52-55; EnvGinMode = "GIN_MODE" at 17). SetMode falls back to test mode under go test (flag test.v) or to debug mode for an empty value, stores debugCode/releaseCode/testCode atomically in ginMode, panics on an unknown value and records the name (58-78). IsDebugging reads ginMode (debug.go:22-24, related). Note that several files define an init function (codec/json/*.go, context_appengine.go); only mode.go's is the answer. Wrong but plausible: debugPrintWARNINGNew (only prints the 'export GIN_MODE=release' hint), IsDebugging / Mode (read the stored mode), DisableBindValidation further down mode.go.

questions.question: I registered `/users`, and a GET to `/users/` gets a 301 redirect to `/users`. Where is that redirect decided and performed?
questions.notes: node.getValue returns tsr=true when the path only differs from a registered route by a trailing slash (for this case tree.go:485). handleHTTPRequest calls redirectTrailingSlash when value.tsr and engine.RedirectTrailingSlash are set, the method is not CONNECT and the path is not '/' (gin.go:755-759, given as lines inside Engine.handleHTTPRequest); RedirectTrailingSlash is true by default in New (224). redirectTrailingSlash adds or strips the trailing slash, prefixing a sanitized X-Forwarded-Prefix (810-824), and redirectRequest answers 301 for GET and 307 for other methods (849-861). Wrong but plausible: redirectFixedPath / node.findCaseInsensitivePath (RedirectFixedPath, off by default), cleanPath (RemoveExtraSlash), Context.Redirect (redirects a handler asks for).

questions.question: When I redirect the server's stdout to a file, the request log lines lose their colors. Where does the logger decide whether to color its output?
questions.notes: LoggerWithConfig sets isTerm=false once, when the middleware is built, if the output is not an *os.File, TERM=dumb, or the descriptor is neither a terminal nor a Cygwin terminal (go-isatty; logger.go:258-263), and copies isTerm into every LogFormatterParams (289-293). IsOutputColor is true for forceColor, or for autoColor when isTerm (162-164); defaultLogFormatter (a var holding a func literal, 167-194, given as lines) fills the color codes only when it is true (169-174). ForceConsoleColor / DisableConsoleColor switch the global mode (197-204). Wrong but plausible: StatusCodeColor / MethodColor / LatencyColor (choose which color, not whether), debugPrint and the [GIN-debug] output.

questions.question: How does gin decide whether to parse the request body as JSON, XML or form data when I call `c.ShouldBind(&obj)`?
questions.notes: ShouldBind and Bind call binding.Default(c.Request.Method, c.ContentType()) (context.go:779-782, 860-863). Default returns Form for every GET, otherwise switches on the MIME type: JSON, XML (two types), ProtoBuf, MsgPack (two types), YAML (two types), TOML, multipart -> FormMultipart, BSON, and Form for anything else (binding.go:95-120). binding_nomsgpack.go is the nomsgpack build-tag twin without MsgPack (91-114); either answers. ContentType cuts parameters such as '; charset=utf-8' with filterFlags (utils.go:92-99). Wrong but plausible: Context.ShouldBind (only delegates), Context.NegotiateFormat (Accept negotiation for the response), the MIME constants at the top of binding.go.

questions.question: json icin encoding/json yerine jsoniter ya da sonic kullanmak istiyorum; gin hangi json kutuphanesini kullanacagini nerede seciyor?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('JSON için encoding/json yerine jsoniter ya da sonic kullanmak istiyorum; gin hangi JSON kütüphanesini kullanacağını nerede seçiyor'). The choice is made at compile time by build tags: json.go is built unless jsoniter, go_json, or sonic on linux/windows/darwin is set (its //go:build line 5), and each variant's init assigns its adapter to the package-level json.API (json.go:17-19, jsoniter.go:18-20, sonic.go:18-20, go_json.go:18-20). All JSON rendering and binding go through json.API (render/json.go:69, binding/json.go:45). Given as lines (build line through init) because the decision is the //go:build constraint plus init, not one symbol; any of the four files answers. Wrong but plausible: api.go Core (only the interface; the API variable is at api.go:10), EnableJsonDecoderUseNumber in mode.go, render.WriteJSON (a user of json.API).

questions.question: router.Static ile bir klasoru sunarken dizin listeleme nasil kapatiliyor?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('router.Static ile bir klasörü sunarken dizin listeleme nasıl kapatılıyor'). Static calls StaticFS(relativePath, Dir(root, false)) (routergroup.go:232-234); Dir wraps http.Dir in OnlyFilesFS unless listDirectory is true (fs.go:42-50); OnlyFilesFS.Open returns every file as a neutralizedReaddirFile (18-25) whose Readdir always returns nil, so http.FileServer gets nothing to list (33-36). createStaticHandler also pre-sets a 404 status when the file system is an *OnlyFilesFS (routergroup.go:257-259; gin's responseWriter only records it until something is written), related. Wrong but plausible: createStaticHandler alone (existence check, then http.FileServer), internal/fs FileSystem (adapts http.FileSystem to fs.FS for LoadHTMLFS), StaticFile (a single file).

questions.question: Struct tag'inde `form:"page,default=1"` yazdığımda, sorguda `page` yoksa varsayılan değer nerede okunup alana yazılıyor?
questions.notes: tryToSetValue splits the tag at commas, records default=... in setOptions (isDefaultExists, defaultValue) and, for slice/array fields with an empty, multi or csv collection_format, turns ';' into ',' (form_mapping.go:159-177), then calls setter.TrySet. setByForm uses opt.defaultValue when the key is missing or its first value is empty (308-309; for slices and arrays the default is split on ',' at 253-264 and 278-289) and passes it to setWithProperType. Wrong but plausible: Context.DefaultQuery (a handler-side helper, unrelated to struct tags), validator rules in the binding tag, mapping (only walks the struct fields).

questions.question: Walk me through what happens between `Engine.ServeHTTP` receiving a request and my handler running: where is the route looked up for the request path, and where are the matched handlers started?
questions.notes: ServeHTTP updates the route trees once (routeTreesUpdated), takes a Context from engine.pool, resets the writer and the Context, calls handleHTTPRequest and puts the Context back (gin.go:691-704). handleHTTPRequest picks the path (URL.Path, or EscapedPath / RawPath depending on options, cleanPath when RemoveExtraSlash), finds the tree for the method and calls root.getValue (719-744); when handlers are found it stores c.Params, c.handlers and fullPath, runs c.Next() and then WriteHeaderNow (745-753); otherwise trailing-slash / fixed-path redirects, 405 and 404 (755-788). node.getValue walks the radix tree, fills params for :name and *catch-all segments, backtracks through skippedNodes and sets the tsr hint (tree.go:418-672). Wrong but plausible: Engine.Run (only starts the http.Server), RouterGroup.handle / node.addRoute (registration time, not request time), Engine.HandleContext (re-entry).

questions.question: When I call `c.ShouldBindJSON(&req)` on a struct with `binding:"required"` tags, how does the body get decoded and then validated?
questions.notes: ShouldBindJSON -> ShouldBindWith(obj, binding.JSON) -> b.Bind(c.Request, obj) (context.go:889-891, 941-943). jsonBinding.Bind rejects a nil request or body and calls decodeJSON (json.go:33-38), which decodes with json.API.NewDecoder, honouring EnableDecoderUseNumber and EnableDecoderDisallowUnknownFields, then calls validate(obj) (44-56). validate skips when binding.Validator is nil (binding.go:122-127); defaultValidator.ValidateStruct validates structs and pointers to structs and every element of slices and arrays, collecting a SliceValidationError (default_validator.go:47-76); validateStruct / lazyinit hand the struct to go-playground/validator configured with tag name 'binding' (79-98). Wrong but plausible: Context.BindJSON / MustBindWith (the aborting 400 variant), ShouldBindBodyWith (caches the body, BindBody path), binding.Default (not used here, the binding is fixed).

questions.question: `v1 := r.Group("/v1", authMiddleware)` ile grup oluşturup `v1.GET("/users", handler)` dediğimde, grubun öneki ve middleware'i bu route'a nasıl ekleniyor ve route ağaca nasıl kaydediliyor?
questions.notes: Group returns a new RouterGroup whose Handlers are the parent's handlers followed by the given middleware (combineHandlers) and whose basePath is the joined path (routergroup.go:96-102). GET calls handle, which computes the absolute path with calculateAbsolutePath / joinPaths, prepends the group's handlers with combineHandlers (a fresh copy, asserted to stay below abortIndex) and calls engine.addRoute (110-115, 277-284). Engine.addRoute asserts the path and handlers, prints the route in debug mode, gets or creates the method tree, inserts the path with node.addRoute and updates maxParams / maxSections (gin.go:387-409). Wrong but plausible: RouterGroup.Use (appends to an existing group, affects only routes registered afterwards), Engine.Use (also rebuilds the 404/405 chains), node.addRoute alone (the tree insert, knows nothing about groups).

questions.question: Where are validation rules like `binding:"required,email"` or `min=3` actually checked against the field values?
questions.notes: The rules (required, email, min, ...) are implemented in go-playground/validator/v10. gin only creates the engine with validator.New() and SetTagName("binding") (default_validator.go:93-98) and calls v.validate.Struct(obj) (79-82); ValidateStruct only dispatches by kind. Custom rules are registered on the engine returned by binding.Validator.Engine() (88-91). Correct behaviour: say the rule checks are not in the repo and cite the pointer. Wrong but plausible: defaultValidator.ValidateStruct (no rule logic), mapping / setByForm in form_mapping.go (parse values, do not validate), SliceValidationError.

questions.question: When I serve files with `c.File` or `router.Static`, where are `Range` requests (206 Partial Content) and `If-Modified-Since` / 304 Not Modified handled?
questions.notes: gin has no range or conditional-request code: Context.File calls http.ServeFile (context.go:1341), FileFromFS and the Static handler hand the request to http.FileServer (1352; routergroup.go:254, 273), and net/http's file serving handles Range, If-Modified-Since, ETag preconditions and 304. Correct behaviour: say it is not in the repo and cite the pointer. Wrong but plausible: bodyAllowedForStatus (only knows that 304 has no body), createStaticHandler (only checks that the file opens), render.Reader / Context.DataFromReader (sets Content-Length, no ranges).

questions.question: HTTP/3 icin QUIC baglantisi, UDP paketleri ve stream yonetimi gin'de nerede yapiliyor?
questions.notes: Turkish without Turkish letters ('HTTP/3 için QUIC bağlantısı, UDP paketleri ve stream yönetimi gin'de nerede yapılıyor'). QUIC and HTTP/3 are implemented by github.com/quic-go/quic-go; gin's only use is RunQUIC, which calls http3.ListenAndServeQUIC(addr, certFile, keyFile, engine.Handler()) (gin.go:658-669; import at 21). Correct behaviour: say it is not in the repo and cite the pointer. Wrong but plausible: Engine.Handler (wraps the engine in h2c for cleartext HTTP/2 when UseH2C is set, 257-264), Engine.RunTLS (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over TLS through net/http).
